citation.title: PyTOaCNN: Topology optimization using an adaptive convolutional neural network in Python
citation.venue: arXiv preprint; later published in Soft Computing

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For the mid-load case, the CNN outputs have small objective and volume differences from designs generated by the classical top88 code; Table 1 reports 1.65% objective error and 5.4% volume error at volume fraction 0.05.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No classical runtime or numerical speed-up is reported; Section 7.1.1 calls CNN output a fraction of a second.
claim.alternatives: Abstract and Section 8 say trained inference is instantaneous; Tables 2-7 give further objective and volume errors against top88, TOPress and topX.

baseline.classical_method: top88 for constant-load compliance, TOPress for pressure loading, and topX for bulk-modulus microstructures (Section 5)
baseline.implementation: Open-source MATLAB codes top88, TOPress and topX (Section 5)
baseline.classical_iterations: TOPress maxit=100; stopping rules and counts for other codes not stated (Section 5)
baseline.ml_time: a fraction of a second, without a numerical value (Section 7.1.1)
baseline.training_time: not stated; 2000 epochs specified in Section 6.5
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; Section 5 reports 95 optimizer-generated training pairs for most cases, and Section 7.1.4 reports 68 for the bulk-modulus case
baseline.quality_metric: Objective error and volume-fraction error, calculated after passing CNN physical densities to the MATLAB optimization codes (Section 7, Tables 1-7)
baseline.quality_gap: At volume fraction 0.05, 1.65% objective error and 5.4% volume error against top88; errors vary by case (Table 1)

R1.evidence: Table 1: the selected quantitative outcome compares design errors, without a measured classical-versus-ML speed comparison.

R2.evidence: Section 5 and Table 1: top88 produces the classical designs; no classical runtime is compared in the selected outcome.

R3.evidence: Abstract, Sections 5-7: the paper claims near-instant trained output, but gives neither total optimization cost for generating training data nor training runtime or break-even analysis.

R4.evidence: Section 7 and Tables 1-7: returned CNN density fields are evaluated using the MATLAB objective codes and volume errors are reported, but disconnected or infeasible output rates are not counted.

reporting.n_test_cases: Tables 1-6: 39 displayed design outputs across four benchmark problem types; Table 7 adds seven volume fractions across six architecture variants [inferred from table rows]

notes: Full text read at https://arxiv.org/html/2404.12244 . Appendix 9 prints model code, but no reusable benchmark data package or measured classical timing was found. Most displayed volume fractions are in the training set; Table 3 tests interpolated unseen fractions.
